title: query a governed open-format dataset through an integrated engine
input: The engineer prepares the supported table format, catalog and approved object-storage dataset.
action: The configured Google Cloud lakehouse architecture combines supported storage, catalog and analytical engines. The selected engine reads table metadata and data files; catalog and storage permissions govern the actual query path.
output: The analyst receives validated aggregates from the selected consistent table snapshot.
check: Check snapshot visibility, schema evolution, engine compatibility and source-access enforcement before publishing results.

title: encode an authorized live feed for adaptive playback
input: The broadcaster prepares an approved input endpoint, channel configuration and output destination.
action: Live Stream API transcodes the configured live input into supported output renditions. Channel settings determine video, audio and packaging outputs; the player or CDN consumes the produced stream.
output: The delivery system serves the accepted manifest and segments and the viewer selects its playback rendition.
check: Test source loss, encoding settings, caption or audio alignment and output access before the event.

title: assess a mainframe estate before choosing a modernization plan
input: The modernization owner provides the supported source inventory and permitted analysis inputs.
action: The assessment tool analyzes supported mainframe artifacts to identify application structure or modernization considerations. Findings inform planning; the tool does not automatically establish business equivalence of a replacement.
output: The migration team groups dependencies and chooses a reviewed modernization approach for each workload.
check: Validate dependency evidence, unsupported components and business-critical transaction coverage before committing the migration plan.

title: transfer a permitted mainframe dataset into a cloud analysis path
input: The mainframe owner selects supported files, encodings and the authorized cloud destination.
action: Mainframe Connector supplies supported integration tooling to transfer or expose selected mainframe data to the configured cloud workflow. Source extraction and encoding conversion must preserve the agreed record semantics.
output: The cloud data job analyzes the accepted dataset and reconciles it with the mainframe source.
check: Check record counts, field encodings, transfer permissions and source timing before using the cloud copy.

title: join an application VM to a managed directory
input: The directory owner selects the domain configuration, permitted network and required trust relationships.
action: Managed Microsoft AD supplies supported managed Active Directory domain capabilities. Joined VMs and applications use the configured directory protocols; cloud IAM access and Windows domain authorization remain separate boundaries.
output: The application authenticates permitted domain users or service accounts through the approved directory path.
check: Test DNS, domain join, trust scope, password policy and denied-user access before application rollout.

title: schedule a retryable nightly warehouse pipeline
input: The data engineer publishes the supported Airflow DAG and restricted task connection settings.
action: The managed Airflow service schedules DAG tasks and runs configured operators in its environment. Those operators invoke the actual extraction or transformation services; Airflow tracks task dependencies and execution state.
output: The final task exposes the accepted warehouse partition after upstream processing and quality gates succeed.
check: Test backfill idempotency, task retry, dependency failure and secret access before enabling the production schedule.

title: buffer order events for independent consumers
input: The order producer publishes an accepted event with a stable identifier to the configured topic.
action: The managed Kafka cluster retains events in configured topic partitions and serves permitted producers and consumers. Consumer groups track their offsets; downstream handlers implement idempotent business updates.
output: The fulfillment consumer processes events and commits offsets after its intended durable completion boundary.
check: Test partition ordering, consumer restart, duplicate effects, topic retention and authentication before production use.

title: prepare plant measurements for a governed manufacturing analysis
input: The manufacturing owner selects permitted equipment sources and agreed asset and timestamp mappings.
action: The configured Manufacturing Data Engine solution ingests and contextualizes supported manufacturing data. Mappings align equipment and process context; downstream analytical code determines the business or maintenance decision.
output: The plant analytics application uses accepted measurements to investigate process variation.
check: Validate equipment identifiers, units, timestamps, missing data and access to proprietary process information.

title: serve licensed video segments from a protected origin
input: The broadcaster publishes accepted video segments and configures the permitted media delivery origin.
action: Media CDN caches and delivers configured content under its origin, routing and cache settings. Delivery does not encode the video; upstream media services create the renditions and playback assets.
output: The authorized player obtains manifests and segments and adapts playback using available renditions.
check: Test origin restrictions, signed access where configured, cache keys and live-segment freshness before launch.

title: cache approved product records with explicit expiry
input: The catalog backend chooses cache keys, expiry and the authoritative product database.
action: Memorystore's selected Valkey offering serves supported in-memory operations under configured cluster and network settings. The backend reads the authoritative database on a miss and refreshes permitted cache entries.
output: The application returns the validated product record and prevents one user's private state from leaking through shared keys.
check: Test cache misses, failover, expiry, reconnect and the exact supported command set before rollout.
